questions.prompt: In ZnO + C → Zn + CO, which substance is the reducing agent?
questions.explain: Carbon takes oxygen from ZnO (and is itself oxidised).

Coating iron with a layer of zinc

questions.prompt: Which change is caused by oxidation of fats?

questions.prompt: In H₂S + Cl₂ → 2HCl + S, which substance is oxidised?
Why do oil-based snacks often contain added antioxidants?
options: To slow down oxidation of the fats

questions.prompt: Explain why oxidation and reduction always happen together, using CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O.
questions.modelAnswer: Oxygen that is removed from one substance must go somewhere. Here CuO loses oxygen (reduction) and that oxygen is gained by hydrogen, forming water (oxidation). So whenever one substance is reduced, another is oxidised: a redox reaction.
rubric: Oxygen transferred, so both happen together
